discovery: The thorium-229 nuclear clock: proposal and laser excitation of the low-energy nuclear isomer transition

nominees.name: Jun Ye
nominees.affiliation: JILA, NIST and University of Colorado Boulder, USA

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / precision metrology
motivation: Peik proposed (2003) using the uniquely low-lying isomer of thorium-229 as an optical clock transition, shielded from environmental perturbations by the atomic shell and highly sensitive to variations of fundamental constants. After two decades of persistent effort, Schumm and Peik's collaboration achieved the first direct laser excitation of this nuclear transition in thorium-doped crystals (2024). Ye's group then linked it phase-coherently to a strontium optical lattice clock via a VUV frequency comb, determining the nuclear frequency with kilohertz-level precision and resolving its quadrupole structure. Together these works turned a spectroscopic curiosity into a new frequency standard that bridges atomic and nuclear physics. The nuclear clock opens unprecedented tests of the constancy of the fine-structure constant and the strong interaction, searches for ultralight dark matter, and robust solid-state timekeeping, a genuinely new instrument for probing nature's laws.
